= GitHub Actions

Use this index to find what starts each workflow, what it does, and where maintainers act.
All jobs run on `ubuntu-latest`.
Jobs that install dependencies use Node.js `26.x` unless listed below.
Claude jobs use `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and make signed commits through the GitHub API.

== Continuous integration

link:ci.yaml[Continuous Integration] runs on pull requests and on pushes to `main` or a `vX.Y.x` maintenance branch.
It installs dependencies, runs `npm run lint:build`, and builds the distribution with `npm run dist`
on Node.js `22.x`, `24.x`, and `26.x`.

== Pull request automation

A _Claude issue PR_ is a pull request Claude opens for an issue from a `claude-issue-<number>-...` branch.
A _Renovate PR_ is a pull request Renovate opens to update a dependency.

=== Claude

link:claude.yaml[Claude] handles maintainer `@claude` requests in issue bodies, comments, and pull request reviews.
A maintainer can also start it by adding the `claude` label to an issue.
For release issues and Publish PRs, use <<publish-pr,Publish PR>>.

Once Claude opens a PR for an issue, post follow-up requests on the PR so Claude can continue on its branch.
A follow-up on the issue prompts Claude to redirect the maintainer to the PR.

Claude and Codex Review share the `claude-<number>` concurrency group to serialize writes to the branch.
For work on an issue or its Claude issue PR, the group uses the issue number.
For other PRs, it uses the pull request number.

=== Renovate and dependency review

The link:../../renovate.json[Renovate configuration] opens one PR per dependency and leaves merging to maintainers.
Its `bump` strategy updates the version range in `package.json` along with the lockfile.
Renovate adds `help wanted` to major, peer dependency, and TypeScript updates.
Use `renovate-regenerate` to have Renovate recreate the branch.

link:dependency-review.yaml[Dependency Review] runs when Renovate opens, reopens, or updates one of its PRs.
Add `claude-review` to rerun the review.
Claude follows the `update-dependency` skill and may push a signed follow-up commit.
A successful run starts Codex Review.

=== Codex review

link:codex-review.yaml[Codex Review] reads new or edited Codex summaries on Renovate PRs and Claude issue PRs.
After a successful Dependency Review run, it reads the latest summary again.

On a Claude issue PR, each distinct commit Codex reviews counts as one round.
On a Renovate PR, reviews through the end of the latest Dependency Review run count together as round 1
when the run succeeded and its commit is still on the PR.
Each later reviewed commit adds a round.
Claude can fix open findings in rounds 1 and 2.
From round 3 onward, the workflow reports any remaining findings.
A failed review or an unreadable summary results in a comment and the `help wanted` label.

=== Codex review watchdog

link:codex-watchdog.yaml[Codex Review Watchdog] checks open Renovate PRs and Claude issue PRs every hour.
Maintainers can also run it manually.
If a PR's latest commit is at least two hours old and has no Codex review,
the workflow comments and adds `help wanted`.
It flags each commit once.

== Releases

A _release issue_ is titled `Release @perfective/build vX.Y.Z`.
A _Publish PR_ comes from the `publish-vX.Y.Z` branch for that release.

[[publish-pr]]
=== Prepare the release PR

To approve a release, add the `claude` label to its open release issue.
link:publish-pr.yaml[Publish PR] prepares a `Publish vX.Y.Z` commit and opens a PR.
The initial commit updates the version in `package.json` and can also update `package-lock.json`,
`CHANGELOG.adoc`, `README.adoc`, `README.md`, and `ROADMAP.adoc`.

To request a fix, re-add `claude` on the release issue or post an `@claude` request on the Publish PR.
The workflow reuses the existing release branch and commits any fixes there.
It stops if the version tag already exists or the Publish PR has been merged.

=== Publish to npm

After merging the Publish PR, the maintainer signs and pushes the release tag.
A push of a `v*` tag starts link:publish.yaml[Publish].
The workflow checks that the tag is annotated, GitHub verifies its signature,
and the tagged commit is on `main` or a `vX.Y.x` maintenance branch.
The version must match `package.json` and have a section in `CHANGELOG.adoc`.

The workflow runs `npm run lint:build` and `npm run dist`, then publishes `./dist` with provenance.
It authenticates to npm through GitHub OIDC and skips versions that npm already has.
The npm dist-tag depends on the release version and branch.

* `next` for a prerelease such as `vX.Y.Z-<id>` on either eligible branch.
* `latest` for a stable release on `main`.
* `backport-X.Y` for a stable release on `vX.Y.x`.

The maintainer creates the GitHub Release manually after npm publishing.
Keep the filename `publish.yaml` because npm trusted publishing is bound to it.
